title: Instrumental Variable Bounds for Selected Target Levels of a Finely Recorded Exposure

proof_attempt_summary: The run derived and audited an exact target-only quotient, a boundary-safe right inverse, finite conditional-experiment factorization for nonempty off-target sets, nuisance-minimax reduction, KL whole-set coverage, and the stated binary witness. It repaired two comparator overclaims and the empty-off-target boundary, after which the same-note math and citation audits passed. The paper still lacked a matched kink minimax/adaptive inference frontier, a matching nonregular rate, scalable computation, and substantive implementation evidence, so D0.5 fixed the contribution at incremental rather than field tier.
tldr: Only selected levels of a finely recorded exposure may define meaningful interventions. Under positive-probability random assignment and exclusion restricted to those levels, the saturated target-only model has an exact quotient: the sharp law of the target potential-outcome vector is the image of a reduced response simplex that keeps target outcome cells and one off-target mass per arm. A boundary-safe right inverse removes the number and labels of off-target categories. For nonempty \(\mathcal C\), conditional on fixed finite arm counts, a rule-specific convexity inequality yields exact equality of the full and skeleton nuisance-minimax values without asserting pointwise risk domination. Separately, a reduced method-of-types confidence region has calibration independent of \( |\mathcal C| \), including the empty-\(\mathcal C\) boundary. The exact kink frontier is left as an open question.
gap: Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjölander's target-level coarsening calculations stop at specified low cardinalities, whereas Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson's adjacent arbitrary-cardinality theory assumes excluded potential outcomes for every exposure category and identifies the larger all-exposure law. Full-alphabet inference consequently confounds scientific target dimension with arbitrary recording detail.
fill: The quotient and its right inverse give sharp identification; the product likelihood and finite-fiber convexification give the exact nuisance-minimax comparison in the conditional finite-count experiment; reduced KL projection gives kink-robust finite-sample coverage; and polyhedral stability converts its radius to a target-set excess bound.
